what: The ball slots (child elements) inside the panel are painted by a shader as a merging color blob that pulls them toward each other — when balls get close a neck forms and joins them, and the edges are slightly distorted like pebbles and wriggle slowly. Move and scale the children with GSAP or CSS and the blob follows, and as the children shrink (1 → .45x), four small balls pop out of each ball, scatter and return

options.[data-fx-part=ball]: Ball slots (children, several) — size, position and opacity are read as they are. Color is that element’s color (style="color: var(--kf-accent)")
options.scatter: Number of scattering small balls, default 4 — 0 means no scatter
options.shrink: Size ratio at which the small balls fully scatter (they all scatter once it shrinks this far from 1), default .55
options.tri: Three-lobe (triangle) distortion strength — the radius swings by 1±tri, default .04. For a .7~1× triangle like the original Brand ball, use .176

note: Load three first so that window.THREE exists (library/_vendor/three@0.177.0 — put this folder’s three-global.js before three.cjs and it is read as window.THREE). Without WebGL it does nothing, so the child image stays visible. The child image is hidden while is-fx-gl is set. If the panel is offscreen it does not draw

from.where: index.html hero color orbs (original MainGL metaball shader — rewritten with our own shader, same formula as kv-gl.js, kv-gl.js uses tri: .176)
